title: What Happens After the Season: Takedown, Storage and Next Year
metaTitle: Holiday Light Takedown, Storage and Next Season
metaDescription: Curious what happens once the season ends? Here is how professional takedown, storage and next year's install work with a full-service lighting company.
excerpt: Booking a professional installer means the lights come down, get inspected and are stored without you lifting a ladder. Here is what actually happens after Twelfth Night, and what to expect heading into next season.
heroAlt: Crew member removing commercial-grade C9 rooflines from a Hamilton home in a boom lift after the holidays
keyTakeaways: A professional takedown is typically scheduled after January 6, respecting the traditional Twelfth Night end of the Christmas season rather than pulling lights down right after New Year's Day.
Every strand, clip and connector comes off the house and goes back with the crew; nothing is left behind for the homeowner to store, and no bin sits in the garage until next November.
Lights and hardware are inspected, tested and repaired in the off-season, not simply boxed up as-is, so next year's install starts with working strands rather than last year's burnouts.

Homeowners who decide they want colour control year-round, not just a seasonal display, can switch to a permanent RGBW system instead of rebooking classic lights.

body.text: The value of hiring a professional holiday lighting company does not end when the lights switch on in November. It shows up again in January, when the season winds down and someone has to get everything off the roof, check it over, and put it away until next year. For a homeowner who installed their own lights, that is the part of the job nobody looks forward to: a cold Saturday on a ladder, tangled strands going into a bin that will sit in the garage for eleven months, and a burnt-out section discovered the following November with no time to fix it. With a full-service installer, none of that falls on the homeowner. Here is what actually happens after the season ends, from takedown day through to next year's install.
Why takedown happens after January 6

Traditionally, the Christmas season runs through Twelfth Night on January 6, and many homeowners in Hamilton, Burlington and across Southern Ontario like to keep their lights up through that date rather than pulling everything down the moment the calendar flips to a new year. Scheduling takedown for after January 6 respects that timeline while still getting lights off the house before the worst of a typical Ontario winter sets in. Crews work through January on a rolling schedule based on when each property was originally installed, so takedown dates are spread out over several weeks rather than everyone competing for the same handful of days right after the holidays.
What happens on takedown day

A takedown crew arrives with the same equipment used for the install, including a boom lift where the roofline needs one, and works through the property in reverse order from how it went up. Rooflines come down first, followed by garland, wreaths and any tree wraps, with every clip and connector removed from the fascia, soffit and gutters along the way. The goal on takedown day is to leave the exterior of the home exactly as it looked before the season started, with no clips, hooks or hardware left behind on the house. Everything, from the bulbs themselves down to the smallest connector, goes back onto the truck with the crew.
Where your lights actually go

Because Festive Holiday Lighting operates as a full-service company rather than a lights-for-sale retailer, there is nothing for a homeowner to buy, unpack, restring or store between seasons. The commercial-grade C9 bulbs, garland, wreaths and connectors used on a property belong to the company's inventory, not to the homeowner, and they travel back to a dedicated storage facility after takedown rather than into a client's basement, garage or attic. That single detail is the difference between a seasonal display and a genuine service: there is no bin taking up space in the garage from January through October, and no scramble the following November to remember which tote the rooflines ended up in.
Inspecting and repairing lights during the off-season

Once lights are back at the storage facility, they do not simply sit untouched until next fall. Each strand is inspected for damaged sockets, worn wiring or bulbs that dimmed or failed partway through the season, since even commercial-grade LEDs occasionally develop a fault after months of exposure to wind, rain and freeze-thaw cycles. Anything that does not pass inspection gets repaired or replaced well before the next install season begins, rather than being discovered halfway up a roofline in November with a client waiting. This is also when connectors, clips and any hardware showing wear get swapped out, so equipment used year after year on client homes stays reliable rather than degrading quietly in the background.
Why this matters compared to store-bought lights

A homeowner storing their own lights rarely has the time or the inclination to test every strand in July. Boxes go into the attic in January and come back out in November, and the first anyone learns about a dead section is when it does not light up on install night. Professional off-season inspection removes that gamble entirely, since the strands arriving at a property each fall have already been tested and repaired months earlier.
What a typical January and February look like behind the scenes

From a homeowner's point of view, the season effectively ends on takedown day. Behind the scenes, that is closer to the midpoint of the annual cycle than the end of it. January and February are when the bulk of the inspection and repair work happens across the full inventory, not just the strands from any one property, since crews are working through every client's lights on a rolling basis rather than all at once. This is also the period when equipment gets sorted and organized ahead of the next design season, so that when a returning client calls in the summer or early fall to confirm their booking, the strands, connectors and hardware for their specific layout are already accounted for rather than being pulled together at the last minute in October.
What changes from one season to the next

Most returning clients keep a similar layout year over year, since the roofline and design that worked well the first season usually still suits the home. That said, plenty of homeowners use the January-to-November gap to think about small changes: adding a tree wrap that was skipped the first year, extending the roofline to cover a garage that was left out originally, or swapping a warm white scheme for something with more colour. Because the property was already measured and photographed during the original install, these changes are usually a quick conversation rather than a full remeasure. Anyone weighing warm white against a multicolour or RGB look for the coming season is welcome to talk it through as part of the free quote process.

Because takedown, inspection and storage all happen behind the scenes, rebooking for the following season is usually the simplest step in the whole process. The roofline measurements, layout and any notes from the previous install are already on file.
Rebooking for next season

Homeowners who want to keep their classic seasonal display running year after year typically hear from Festive Holiday Lighting well before the fall install season fills up, since returning clients are usually offered priority scheduling ahead of new bookings. The process itself is simpler than year one: there is no roofline to measure from scratch, no design to work out from a blank slate, and no need to guess at bulb count or colour temperature, since all of that is already documented from the original install. A quick confirmation of any changes, whether that is a new section of roofline or a different colour scheme, and the property goes back onto the November install schedule. Details on what a seasonal install includes are at /services/christmas-light-installation.
When it makes sense to switch to permanent lighting

After a season or two of classic lights, some homeowners decide they would rather have colour control available year-round rather than only during the holidays, or they simply want to remove the annual install-and-takedown cycle from their calendar entirely. That is exactly the gap permanent lighting fills. A permanent RGBW system goes into a discreet roofline channel once, comes with a lifetime hardware warranty, and switches between a holiday palette, a warm white everyday look, or colours for a birthday or graduation from an app, without a crew needing to come back each November and January. Anyone weighing the two options can compare the ongoing seasonal service against a one-time permanent install at /services/permanent-lighting.
Planning ahead if your needs change

Life circumstances change what makes sense for a property from one year to the next. A family that is renovating or listing a home for sale might pause seasonal lighting for a season, while a homeowner planning to stay put for years might decide it is the right time to move to a permanent system instead of rebooking a classic install. Either way, there is no obligation tied to a previous season's install, and the conversation about what makes sense going forward is part of the same free quote process used for a first-time client. Photos of past seasonal and permanent installs across Hamilton, Burlington, Oakville and the surrounding area are available at /gallery, and a free quote for either option can be requested at /contact or by calling (289) 426-5764.

The short version is that once a homeowner books a professional install, the season effectively runs itself from that point forward. The lights go up in November, get maintained through the season, come down after January 6, get inspected and repaired over the winter, and are ready to go back up the following fall, all without a ladder, a storage bin or a phone call about a burnt-out strand in the middle of December.

faq.a: Takedown is scheduled after January 6, respecting the traditional Twelfth Night end of the Christmas season, and crews work through a rolling schedule over the following weeks based on each property's original install date.

faq.q: Do I need to store any lights or equipment myself?
faq.a: No. Because Festive Holiday Lighting provides a full installation service rather than selling lights, all bulbs, garland, wreaths and hardware belong to the company's inventory and are taken away and stored by the crew after takedown. Nothing is left with the homeowner.

faq.q: What happens if a strand burns out during the season?
faq.a: Maintenance is part of the seasonal service, so a burnt-out section identified during the season is repaired without the homeowner needing to do anything. Any remaining issues are also caught and fixed during the off-season inspection before the next install.

faq.q: Do returning clients need a new quote every year?
faq.a: Not typically. Since the roofline was already measured and the layout documented during the original install, rebooking is usually a quick confirmation of the existing plan or any small changes, rather than a full remeasure and design from scratch.

faq.q: Can I switch from classic lights to a permanent system later?
faq.a: Yes. Many clients start with a seasonal C9 install and later move to a permanent RGBW system once they decide they want year-round colour control without an annual install and takedown. See /services/permanent-lighting for details.

faq.q: How do I get on the schedule for next season?
faq.a: Returning clients are generally given priority scheduling ahead of new bookings as the fall season approaches. New or returning clients can request a free quote at /contact or by calling (289) 426-5764.
